title: Selector Gym — Playwright locator trainer
description: A realistic checkout form rendered as real DOM, paired with a hand-written parser for getByRole, getByLabel, getByText, getByPlaceholder, getByTestId, CSS locator() and chaining. Type an expression and matches light up live; clear ten progressive challenges where role-based answers score full points and CSS answers pass as 'brittle'.
prompt: Build me a 'Selector Gym': a trainer for Playwright locators. Put a believable mock checkout page on the left as real DOM, and on the right an input where I type a locator expression like getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }). Write a small parser and a simplified accessibility model (implicit roles, accessible names from labels, aria-label, legends and content) so getByRole, getByLabel, getByText, getByTestId, getByPlaceholder and locator('css') all work, including chaining, filter({ hasText }), and state options like disabled and checked. Highlight matches live with a count and a Playwright-style list of what matched. Add ten progressive challenges — the disabled Save button, three identical Remove buttons, two City fields that need scoping — with scoring that rewards semantic locators over brittle CSS and hints that explain why.

methodology: Functional: drive the page purely through its own UI — fill the locator input, press Enter or click Check — and assert match count, highlighted elements and score.
Parser robustness: feed malformed input (unclosed braces, unknown methods, invalid CSS) and assert a readable error instead of a thrown exception.
Oracle independence: each challenge's target is resolved from fixed DOM references, not by re-running the engine, so a bug in the matcher can't mark itself correct.
Scoring rules: verify the three credit tiers (10 semantic, 4 CSS, 2 after revealing the answer) and that ambiguous locators fail with a strict-mode explanation.
A11y: the trainer is fully keyboard-driven, results announce through aria-live, and the mock app itself is built with correct labels so the semantic answers genuinely exist.
risks: The simplified accessible-name algorithm drifting from Chromium's (e.g. names from wrapping labels or aria-labelledby), making a 'correct' Playwright locator fail in the gym.
getByText picking an ancestor instead of the innermost element, inflating counts.
Debounced live evaluation racing a Check click, scoring a stale expression.
qa.playwright: This was pleasantly easy to automate because the page is plain DOM with data-testid hooks on every output, so locators like getByTestId('match-count') plus web-first toHaveText assertions absorb the 90 ms input debounce without any sleeps. The interesting part is meta: the spec uses real Playwright locators to verify a toy re-implementation of Playwright locators, and asserting on the [data-gym-hit] attribute inside the mock app checks what was highlighted rather than how it looks. No screenshots were needed — highlight state is an attribute, so visual diffs would add flakiness without adding signal. Tap and click are interchangeable here, so the same spec runs unchanged on the Pixel 7 project.
coverage: Live highlighting and match count for a single and a multi-match role locator
Parser errors for syntax, unknown methods and invalid CSS
Solving a challenge for full points and ladder state
Strict-mode failure for an ambiguous locator, then success with { disabled: true }
CSS answer scored as brittle, then upgraded via a scoped chain
Show answer fills the input and caps credit

a11y: Every trainer control is a real button or labelled input, Enter submits a check, and match counts and feedback are announced through aria-live regions. The mock checkout is built with proper labels, legends and aria-labels, and the ladder buttons expose each challenge's status in their accessible names.
